#2703. Rockets snag 115-108 win over shorthanded Warriors

The Houston Rockets will always take a victory over the Golden State Warriors, even when the Dubs are shorthanded, and that's exactly what happened on Wednesday night. Stephen Curry went down in the first quarter and did not return, setting the table for a Rockets victory. And while Houston did make it much closer than it needed to be, the Dubs didn't quite have the firepower without Steph to hang with the Rockets down the stretch, and despite a couple close Q4 -pushes by Golden State, the Rockets walked away with a 115-108 victory to move to 9-3 on the season.

The Rockets were led by Kevin Durant with 20 points, as all five Houston starters finished in double in figures. KD also had 4 rebounds and 5 assists. Alperen Sengun was near-miss on a triple double, finishing with 19 points, 13 rebounds, and 9 assists while shooting 8-for-14 from the field. Houston also got 19 from Amen Thompson, who finally had a decent offensive game, shooting 8-for-11. He also added 7 rebounds, 4 assists, a steal and 2 blocks for the kind of all-around performance we've been missing from Amen. Houston also 18 points and 6 assists from Fed VanVleet and 14 points and 8 rebounds from Jabari Smith Jr. to round out the scoring from the starters.

Reed Sheppard pitched in 13 points off the bench on 3-for-6 shooting from deep, and that about ended the bench contributions, as Tari Eason shot just 2-for-11, while Marcus Smart was ejected in the third quarter for throwing a punch. Welcome to the Houston-Golden State rivalry, Marcus. It took all of one half of a game for Smart to want to smack a Dub around. Sheppard had a solid fourth quarter in taking over Smart's minutes.

Houston shot 51 percent in this one, while holding the Warriors to just 41 percent. The Rockets were also hammering the ball inside, as they led in paint scoring 50-34. One of thew few reasons the game was close was the difference in three-point shooting, as Golden State put up 51 threes (making 17) to Houston's 36 attempts (making 13). The Rockets have increased their three attempts so far this season, up to 34.2 per game from 31.5. Accuracy has also increased, up to 37.5 percent from 36.4 perccent. All of that is good. But the Rockets can still find themselves in closer than needed situations when they play teams with a big three-point attempt difference.

Nonetheless, every good NBA season requires a little luck, and I'm certainly not one to feel bad about a Warriors player getting injured against the Rockets, considering the history these two teams have. I'll take the win, and we'll see you again later.

Houston's 9-3 record has moved them back up to third in the Western Conference. They will be back in action on Friday night, with a home game against another historic rival, the Utah Jazz.

#2702. Full-back Barrett leads New Zealand for first time

Full-back Beauden Barrett will captain New Zealand for the first time when he leads out the All Blacks for the Nations Championship game against Wales in Cardiff on Saturday.

All Blacks head coach Dave Rennie has made eight starting changes from the side that defeated Scotland 43-21 at Murrayfield with 10 alterations in the match-day 23.

It will be 35-year-old Barrett's first time as starting skipper in his 149th international with brother Scott also named at lock, while Richie Mo'unga is at fly-half.

"Beauden brings such valuable experience and is massively respected by us all," said Rennie.

"Captaining the All Blacks in a Test is an honour I know he doesn't take lightly, so it'll be a proud day for him and his whanau [family]."

Basham starts for Wales as Wainwright ruled out

Why Wales have a lot to prove despite beating Japan

Smiling Rees-Zammit has no fear of All Blacks

The All Blacks defeated Scotland 43-21 last Saturday, but record try-scoring wing Will Jordan (hamstring) and centre Jordie Barratt (facial) picked up injuries and are absent against Wales.

Flanker Anton Segner and wing Fehi Fineanganofo, whose move to Newcastle Red Bulls in the summer was delayed by a year, make their first Test starts.

Segner, prop George Bower, hooker Asafo Aumua and scrum-half Cortez Ratima move from the replacements into the starting side.

Mo'unga, Fineanganofo, lock Josh Lord and centre Anton Lienert-Brown also come into the side.

"We have created good depth in this group and there is a lot of competition for places," said Rennie.

"We have selected a strong squad with 783 caps."

New Zealand have won the past 34 Tests against Wales in a winning sequence that stretches back to 1953.

"Wales are a proud rugby nation and building nicely under Steve Tandy," said Rennie.

"We are well aware of the threat they pose and the challenge of playing in front of a passionate crowd at Principality Stadium."

New Zealand and South African are currently unbeaten in the southern hemisphere table.

The rivals are battling for top spot before the play-off weekend at the end of the month.

New Zealand: B Barrett (capt); Fineanganofo, Tupaea, Lienert-Brown, Moorby; Mo'unga, Ratima; Bower, Aumua, Newell, S Barrett, Lord, Segner, Lakai, Sititi.

#2701. Week 10 NFL picks against the spread, predictions for every game: Kirk Cousins returns to lead Vikings vs. Packers

It wasn't that long ago that Kirk Cousins, in his first stint with the Minnesota Vikings, was the quarterback who could never win the big one. Everyone remembers this critique of him.

These days, Kirk Cousins is 38. And somehow, everyone spent days and weeks arguing that the only way for the Vikings to have a chance to win the big one was to trade for Cousins.

That trade did happen, and it was perfectly reasonable for the Vikings to see if Cousins can guide them to an NFC North title and maybe a playoff run. They have the defense for it but we saw on Monday night that the offense was beyond repair with the quarterback situation they had. Vikings coach Kevin O'Connell was hesitant to announce Cousins would start Sunday against the Green Bay Packers, but the Vikings didn't trade for Cousins to watch Kyler Murray or Carson Wentz start in a huge divisional game.

While the trade for Cousins was reasonable, the Vikings still have the fourth-best quarterback in the division and the fourth-best offense in the division as well. Cousins is an upgrade but mostly because the Vikings had a dreadful quarterback situation.

The Packers didn't do anything at the trade deadline but it might be because they've been on quite a roll. They were not good through three weeks but somehow have emerged as one of the better teams in the NFL since then. Since Week 4, they're fourth in EPA (expected points added) per play on offense and third in EPA per play allowed on defense. It's a good team.

Anyone will have issues with the Vikings' defense and we'll see if the Packers' deep passing game can function against Minnesota's many blitzes. But Packers -3 is the pick. Taking the Vikings and Cousins, five days after rejoining the team, against a red-hot team is too much to ask.

New Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kirk Cousins (8) shown facing the Packers in a 2023 game.

Here are the rest of the picks against the spread for Week 10 of the NFL season:

The Giants are three games up on the Commanders in the NFC East, but New York isn't that great. The Commanders come in as the more desperate team. Their season is all but over if they lose on Thursday. That's not the best reason to pick a team, but it's good enough in a game between two flawed teams.

This is the NFL's last early-morning game of the season. The Lions and Patriots meet in Germany. The Patriots are coming off a bad loss to the Packers, and have their running back issues with Rhamondre Stevenson and TreVeyon Henderson out. One factor to consider is the Lions aren't the same team outdoors. Jared Goff's rating in domes is 102.9 and outdoors it is 92.4. There is some noise in those numbers, and Goff's ratings haven't had that big of a gap the past two seasons, but Detroit also just scored 19 points at Miami last week. That and the Lions' defensive deficiencies are enough to take the Patriots and the points.

The Browns have a better record, but also a -35 point differential. It's not like the Texans have been great, but there's a path for them to make the playoffs. They also know they can't drop games like this one. C.J. Stroud is playing well enough that points shouldn't be too hard for Houston to come by.

The Jaguars have taken over as my Super Bowl pick after the deadline. However, 10.5 is a lot of points in the NFL and the Titans have played three close games in a row. They're coming off their bye and have some extra rest. The Jaguars can't blow everyone out, right?

It's very hard to take the Colts, especially because the Dolphins are playing hard. The Colts played hard last week, but have to be deflated after losing that game to the Cowboys in the final minutes and seeing more players traded away. But it's even harder to back new Dolphins quarterback Kyle McCord, a 2025 sixth-round pick who has never taken an NFL snap, playing with a subpar group. McCord gets the start for Miami with Malik Willis on injured reserve.

Talk about an ugly NFL side to take. The Jets are not good. But the Bills are coming off a physical game in Minnesota on Monday night and now go on the road to face the Jets on short rest. It seems unwise to take the Jets, but point spreads exist for a reason.

The Saints are probably better in theory than reality. They won last week, but needed to defend a two-point conversion in overtime to knock off Shedeur Sanders and the Browns. It feels like the Saints have the potential to be the best team in the NFC South, but there's not much evidence they are. The Panthers are in a slump but have been the better team.

It's not like the Falcons trading Jessie Bates III makes them significantly worse, but it's a difficult message for the locker room. It makes it seem like the front office is waving the white flag. In reality they got an offer they couldn't turn down, but it's still worth wondering how the remaining players will react. And Kansas City is a pretty good team.

For the rest of the season, or at least until Puka Nacua or Davante Adams returns, the Rams will try to survive by running the ball and playing defense in low-scoring games. There's not much explosiveness in the offense without any dangerous receivers. That will make them tough to back when the spread is large. Can Carson Beck lead the Arizona offense to enough points against a good Rams defense to cover any spread? That's the key question.

This isn't a pick due to Fernando Mendoza facing the Seahawks defense, though that is a factor. It's because the Raiders defense is horrible. Since Week 3, after the Raiders had faced the offensively challenged Dolphins and Chargers, they're last in the NFL in EPA by a wide margin. They're 32nd in yards allowed and points allowed. The Seahawks will be able to move the ball, even with Drew Lock at quarterback.

There are no signs the Cowboys are ready to have some kind of breakout. Last week they almost lost to a Colts team that has already given up on the season. And now they're supposed to keep it close against the 49ers, who have arguably been the best team in the NFL?

The Joe Burrow-for-MVP bandwagon is still running, but it's hard to lay more than a field goal in what should be a great divisional game. The Steelers can run the ball, and run defense is a weakness of the Bengals. They're last in the NFL in yards allowed per carry. Also, the Steelers are coming off a bye while the Bengals are coming off a game in Paris, which is the type of massive rest disadvantage that the NFL should do a better job avoiding. The Bengals are good but this isn't a great matchup or a good spot for them.

The Chargers will cover a spread this season. They haven't yet. They are the last team in the NFL to not cover the spread this season. But we'll take that loss when it comes because proactively taking the truly miserable Chargers in hopes they finally cover is not an enjoyable exercise. Also, the Ravens have three days of extra rest and perhaps a little bit of renewed hope with Jacoby Brissett coming aboard.

#2699. NHL Rumours: Montreal Canadiens Hoping to Sell High On Oliver Kapanen

NHL rumours continue to knock on the door of the Montreal Canadiens, with the latest revolving around players who may be moved as regular roster players return to health. According to one pundit, the Habs have identified the player they would like to sell high on. Without further ado, let's get into the details.

Rumour: On Tuesday, on the Starr and D'Amico Show, a discussion unfolded about players returning to health for the Montreal Canadiens. They noted the roster clog that will result when everyone is healthy, and that based on how a couple of guys have been playing, there is an opportunity to sacrifice quantity for quality. Marco D'Amico said that from what he has been hearing, Oliver Kapanen is the player that the Canadiens are trying to sell high on at this point based on his play last season.

Analysis: As injured players return to health, the Canadiens will have to concern themselves with both roster spots and staying within the 23-man limit, and managing their cap space. While key players have been away, youngsters have proven themselves, and their presence will force management to assess their best options moving forward, and to use some of their extras as trade chips to upgrade their roster. Kapanen is a young player with value that can be packaged for that purpose.

D'Amico discussed the issue that arises when Ivan Demidov returns to action, which is expected to happen in the near future. According to NHL rumours, the Montreal Canadiens have been trying to acquire a top-six asset to complement Demidov dating back to last trade deadline when they tried to acquire Matthew Knies, and in the summer when they pursued Kirill Marchenko, and more recently in their inquiries about Dylan Larkin.

According to D'Amico, the Canadiens are hoping teams would see in Kapanen a player that can shine as a complement to skilled players, as he did with Demidov last season. In his efforts to acquire a top-six player, Hughes is hoping Kapanen can be a key piece in a package. D'Amico also mentioned Kirby Dach's contract as an option to move to create cap space to acquire that player. Dach's name has been in rumours previously, and with his improved play of late, and this may increase the chances of such a deal.

Sep 28, 2022; Toronto, Ontario, CAN; Montreal Canadiens goalie Samuel Montembeault (35) makes a glove save against the Toronto Maple Leafs in the second period at Scotiabank Arena. Mandatory Credit: Dan Hamilton-USA TODAY Sports | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Alec Roberson

Perhaps the most controversial player returning to health, and a continued subject of NHL rumours, is goaltender Sam Montembeault. The Montreal Canadiens approached the season with a netminder conundrum. They had three NHL-ready goalies and multiple options to address their crowded net. Ultimately, the decision was made to loan Jacob Fowler to the Laval Rocket, and to run a tandem of Montembeault and Jakub Dobes, who had won the starter's net last season. But Montembeault was injured early, and Fowler called up to replace him.

Fowler has been excellent in relief, and the belief is that the Habs are not prepared to demote him again. Now Montembeault is near ready to return and decisions await. On Tuesday, General Manager Kent Hughes disclosed to the media that they may have Montembeault complete a conditioning stint in Laval before returning to Montreal.

D'Amico addressed this in the podcast, noting that they could place Montembeault on retroactive injury relief and he would be eligible for such a conditioning stint if the player was open to the arrangement. No doubt Montembeault will be open to any steps that would get him closer to regular playing time in the NHL.

On Wednesday morning on The Morning Show on TSN690, Darren Dreger discussed what he was hearing about Montembeault. He said he knew Hughes had been having conversations with clubs that had inquired about the veteran goalie in the past few weeks. He confirmed there was interest in Montembeault, but he wasn't sure the market was strong just yet. Dreger was asked if a couple of strong games in Laval might be enough to generate interest, and he said it might be. Certainly, the Habs would like to find a new home for Montembeault, and removing his contract would provide cap space for future moves.

The Montreal Canadiens have already traded one defenceman this season, when they dealt Jayden Struble to Nashville. There have also been NHL rumours of Adam Engstrom being showcased, and of Montreal's interest in Simon Edvinsson out of Detroit. Prospect David Reinbacher is also playing very well in Laval. With Mike Matheson close to a return, NHL rumours are circulating about whether a Montreal Canadiens defender may be close to a trade.

Earlier in the week, Hockey Insider Frank Seravalli joined Flames Now with Pat Steinberg and discussed the season-ending injury to Kevin Bahl, and Calgary's search for help on defence. He immediately mentioned the Montreal Canadiens depth on defence as an option for Calgary. D'Amico discussed the awkwardness of sending one of the young players who are performing well to Laval when Matheson returns, mentioning Engstrom, along with Owen Beck and Florian Xhekaj.

The Montreal Canadiens continue to be at the centre of NHL rumours. With their strong start to the season, despite multiple injuries, and with the glut of prospects who are forcing their way into permanent roles, the Habs have decisions to make as players return to health. The return of each of Demidov, Montembeault and Matheson all trigger decision points for the Habs, and opportunities to further shape their roster as they rise to contention.

#2693. For the Wizards, it’s not as early as we think.

Okay, now I'm worried. The Wizards went to Indiana and got thumped by a Tyrese Haliburton-less Pacers team. It's Washington's fifth straight loss — and four of the five have been by 10 points or more.

If you want to stick to the "it's early" and "they're finding their way and they'll improve as the season goes on" talking points, you'll probably want to skip a few paragraphs. Because I did some looking up and some numbers crunching, and…well…it's not as early as you think. I mean, I was getting nervous when the streak reached three, and I was reciting those Talking Points myself, so let me be clear — it's not as early as I was thinking.

Wizards guard Tre Johnson played one of his better games of the season in the team's loss to the Indiana Pacers. | NBAE via Getty Images

The Wizards entered last night's game against the Pacers with a strength of schedule adjusted scoring -11.3 through 11 games. They lost by 13 to a team scoring a -6.3 in the same metric. That's not good. And the team's performance a dozen games into the season is greater cause for worry than I'd imagined.

While it feels early, analysis of NBA history says that by this point in the season, we already have about half the information needed to determine a team's relative strength in the league. Even just 8-10 games is enough to be more than just random noise.

There's still some noise — early-season blowouts have bigger impacts on this type of scoring differential metric than it will by the end of the season — but what we see in the first month of the season is a surprisingly good indicator of what we're going to see over the final five.

In the case of the Wizards this season, they may not really be the quality of a team that wins just 14-15 games (which is what their adjusted scoring margin implies), but a) they could be, and b) it's pretty unlikely they're even the quality of a 35-win team. Best case at this point is probably mid-20s in wins — better than last season, though not the major step forward many hoped.

While it's not as early as we think, it's getting later fast. We already have half the information needed to draw a meaningful conclusion. By game 20, it'll be about 70%. By game 30, it's closing in on 80%.

Perhaps the biggest wildcard in all this is the role of three-point shooting luck. According to research published on the Above the Break Substack, it takes about 33 games for opponent three-point shooting to stabilize. Unfortunately, opponent three-point shooting reverting to the mean could be brutal for Washington — so far this season opponents have been laying bricks from deep.

Of course, reversion could also benefit the Wizards on offense — they've been shooting slightly worse from the arc than their opponents. The likely outcome is reversion effects cancel each other out, and Washington ends up basically where they are now, albeit looking a bit better on offense and a bit worse on defense.

None of this is writ in stone, of course. There are examples of teams in NBA history that overcame a rough first month to become good. But it's rare. And usually those teams aren't as deep in the scoring margin hole as the Wizards are. I mean, the Sacramento Kings have been a 1-9 horror show this season, and their adjusted scoring margin is better than Washington's.

Now, it's not all doom and gloom. The Wizards rank 26th in adjusted scoring margin, but the four teams even worse are all in the Eastern Conference. It's conceivable that the Wizards could continue playing just as bad and still make the play-in thanks to the struggles of the Brooklyn Nets, Milwaukee Bucks, Charlotte Hornets, and Chicago Bulls.

The Pacers announced that Haliburton — the team's best player — will miss at least another 10 days with his hamstring injury. He's been one of my favorite watches since he entered the NBA, and he looked fantastic in his first four games back from the Achilles injury.

On a first quarter drive, AJ Dybantsa made Kelly Oubre Jr. — known for his athleticism — look slow. Oubre actually looked startled at how sudden Dybantsa was.

A first quarter sequence underscored how much work Tre Johnson needs to do on his body and his overall game. T.J. McConnell wrecked a Washington possession by denying Johnson the ball. The denial forced Davis to handle out top. After setting a half-hearted screen for Davis, Johnson kinda stood around waiting. Davis tried to throw the ball to him, McConnell stole the pass — I mean, HE WAS STANDING IN THE PASSING LANE — and then led the fastbreak, which resulted in a wide open three for Obi Toppin.

That play aside, Johnson played one of his better games of the season. One play design I liked — early in the the second quarter, the Wizards screened for him in the weakside corner. It looked kind of like a traditional pindown action, except Johnson came to the ball for a dribble handoff that gave him a wide open three-point attempt. He missed, but the design and execution was good.

Two thoroughly disgusting defensive plays in the second quarter: On the first, Oubre got a dunk because Bub Carrington turned his back on him to watch a drive on the opposite side of the floor. Oubre noticed the turned head and cut behind him for the slam. On the second, Oubre got another dunk because Young tried to cheat the screen on a sideline out of bounds play — guessing that Oubre would come off the screens towards the ball. Oubre went weak side and was wide open.

Learning moment for Dybantsa — he dribbled too high while trying to back down Oubre and got picked clean for a breakaway dunk.

If all you look at is The Glory Stats, Kyshawn George looks really good last night — 25 points, 9 rebound, 3 assists. Heck, he even shot 5-8 from three-point range. So why does he end up with a below-average score in my PPA metric? He shot 4-12 on twos, committed six turnovers, and contributed to a worse-than-average team defense.

Below are the four factors that decide wins and losses in basketball — shooting (efg), rebounding (offensive rebounds), ball handling (turnovers), fouling (free throws made).

eFG% (effective field goal percentage, which accounts for the three-point shot)

TOV% (turnover percentage — turnovers divided by possessions)

FTM/FGA (free throws made divided by field goal attempts)

PPA is my overall production metric, which credits players for things they do that help a team win (scoring, rebounding, playmaking, defending) and dings them for things that hurt (missed shots, turnovers, bad defense, fouls).

PPA is a per possession metric designed for larger data sets. In small sample sizes, the numbers can get weird. In PPA, 100 is average, higher is better and replacement level is 45. For a single game, replacement level isn't much use, and I reiterate the caution about small samples sometimes producing weird results.

POSS is the number of possessions each player was on the floor in this game.

ORTG = offensive rating, which is points produced per individual possessions x 100. League average so far this season is listed in the Four Factors table above. Points produced is not the same as points scored. It includes the value of assists and offensive rebounds, as well as sharing credit when receiving an assist.

USG = offensive usage rate. Average is 20%. Median last season was 17.7%.

ORTG and USG are versions of stats created by former Wizards assistant coach Dean Oliver and modified by me. ORTG is an efficiency measure that accounts for the value of shooting, offensive rebounds, assists and turnovers. USG includes shooting from the floor and free throw line, offensive rebounds, assists and turnovers.

+PTS = "Plus Points" is a measure of the points gained or lost by each player based on their efficiency in this game compared to league average efficiency on the same number of possessions. A player with an offensive rating (points produced per possession x 100) of 100 who uses 20 possessions would produce 20 points. If the league average efficiency is 115, the league — on average — would produced 23.0 points in the same 20 possessions. So, the player in this hypothetical would have a +PTS score of -3.0.

Players are sorted by total production in the game.

#2691. College football Week 11 what to watch: It's the last stand for LSU's playoff hopes in Lane Kiffin's first season

The sprint to the finish of the 2026 college football regular season is here.

Week 11 features five games between teams in the top 25 of the College Football Playoff rankings and a host of other games between ranked teams and opponents who aren't that far outside the rankings. Here's what you need to know ahead of Saturday's slate.

We were surprised to see the Blue Devils unranked in Tuesday night's CFP rankings.

Yes, Duke's two losses are to Georgia Tech and North Carolina, and yes, their last two games were against Boston College and NC State. But two wins by a combined score of 88-5 is impressive, no matter who the opponents are.

There are only two power conference teams who are 7-2 and unranked in the CFP's rankings. Both are in the ACC. SMU is also 7-2.

Saturday's game is the chance for more college football fans to learn about Nate Sheppard's greatness. The Duke running back has 191 carries for 1,189 yards and 17 scores. And there are still three games to go in the regular season. After four consecutive games with fewer than 100 yards, Sheppard had 18 carries for 217 yards and three touchdowns against NC State. He has eight rushing TDs over the past two games.

Miami is looking to rebound after its loss to Notre Dame. It took a while for Cooper Barkate and Elija Lofton to emerge against the Fighting Irish as Darian Mensah had his worst passing game of the season. Can the Hurricanes lean into the run game more than they did against Notre Dame? Javian Mallory had just three carries for 14 yards, while Mark Fletcher rushed 13 times for 57 yards.

If Miami gets the win, the Hurricanes can be on the brink of the ACC title game. Duke would have a third ACC loss and Wake Forest will either have two losses or SMU will have a third conference loss.

Can USC do something it's never done in Lincoln Riley's time with the Trojans?

Riley's USC teams have never beaten a ranked opponent on the road outside of Los Angeles. Over Riley's four-plus seasons in LA, the only win over a ranked opponent on the road came in 2022, when USC beat then-No. 16 UCLA 48-45 at the Rose Bowl. Outside of those games, USC is 0-7 as the visiting team against a team in the AP Top 25.

Both the Trojans and Hoosiers are coming off bye weeks. Week 10 was USC's second of the season after it played in Week Zero. Through three trips to the Central and Eastern Time zones this season, USC is 2-1 with one-score wins over Rutgers and Penn State, and an ugly 24-7 loss at Wisconsin.

Of course, USC rebounded after that Wisconsin game to take down Ohio State and immediately jump back into the top 25. Big plays fueled that win and it's unlikely that USC can count on replicating that formula against an Indiana defense that's been one of the best in the country — and can rush the passer better than Ohio State has this season.

The Hoosiers could start QB Grant Wilson after he took over in the second half for a banged-up Josh Hoover in the overtime win over Minnesota. No matter who starts at quarterback, we expect Indiana to try to overpower a USC defense that's giving up nearly 125 yards a game on the ground. Indiana's run game is still one of the best in the country despite the struggles through the air.

Could the Big 12 title race get thrown into chaos on Saturday night? Wins by Arizona and Oklahoma State could put a huge wrench in a potential Utah vs. Texas Tech matchup in Arlington.

As it stands entering Saturday, Utah is atop the conference with a 6-0 record, while Texas Tech is 5-1. After them, there are five teams at 4-2: BYU, Houston, Arizona, Baylor and Oklahoma State. That group could increase to six, and all of them could be just a game back of the Utes.

How much of a letdown spot is this game for the Utes, who have taken down two ranked opponents and a Cincinnati team fresh off a win over the Red Raiders across the last three weeks? In the biggest Holy War to date, Utah jumped out to a big lead and then needed to come back from a BYU comeback to beat the Cougars 28-20.

A win over Arizona and a strong game from QB Devon Dampier can vault him into the Heisman conversation. Dampier has thrown for 20 scores and run for seven others while completing 68% of his passes.

After a loss at Texas Tech, Arizona needed some late-game wildness to overcome an eight-point deficit in the fourth quarter to beat TCU 29-28. The Wildcats are still dangerous, and Noah Fifita could be the best quarterback the Utes have played all season. He's completing 73% of his passes and has thrown for over 300 yards in each of Arizona's past four games.

LSU's playoff hopes are officially gone with a loss to the Longhorns, while Texas appears to be able to withstand a defeat and still make the postseason.

Texas moved up a spot to No. 6 after beating Missouri and the Tigers remained in the CFP's rankings. That's significant, as Texas can now boast four wins over teams in this week's top 25. A fifth win Saturday night almost assures Texas of a playoff spot even if the Longhorns lose to either Arkansas or Texas A&M over the final two weeks of the season.

LSU, meanwhile, is on the brink of missing the playoff in Lane Kiffin's first season and, if you really want to be pessimistic, is closer to 7-5 than it is to making the postseason. We're fascinated to see how aggressive Kiffin is against a very good Texas defense after his fourth-down failures against Alabama. LSU was 0-of-4 on fourth-down attempts in the loss to the Crimson Tide. Will he be dissuaded, especially if he faces an early fourth-down decision?

The Longhorns could have Cam Coleman back after he sat out the Missouri game and should have a healthier Colin Simmons. The star edge rusher tried to give it a go in his first game back from an ankle injury, but ended up sitting out the second half against Mizzou. No opposing offense has averaged over 6 yards a play against LSU all season, and none of the Tigers' last three opponents have accumulated over 300 yards.

Yet LSU has also forced just one turnover in that span. The Tigers may need a couple from Arch Manning to get the win.

We're prepared for a second straight Texas Tech game to have over 100 total points.

In Week 10, Texas Tech took down West Virginia 53-48 thanks to a late safety on a sack of Mountaineers QB Michael Hawkins. Oklahoma State, meanwhile, had 49 points in the first half as it beat Kansas State 66-28.

This is not the Texas Tech defense we watched a year ago. While Jacob Rodriguez finished fifth in the Heisman voting and Tech allowed 11.8 points per game last year, the Red Raiders are giving up 24 points per game and 5.6 yards a play in 2026. Tech ranks 65th in opponent points per game.

Former Florida State and Boston College QB Thomas Castellanos has rushed for over 100 yards in each of his two starts since taking over for Will Hammond as Texas Tech's quarterback. Castellanos rushed 23 times for 102 yards and threw for 362 yards and five touchdowns against WVU.

The OSU defense is better than West Virginia's — though that's damning with faint praise. Oklahoma State is 93rd in the country in scoring defense at 27.2 points per game. But if it can slow Castellanos and RB J'Koby Williams down enough, OSU's offense can take advantage.

QB Drew Mestemaker is sneaking up the Heisman odds and has thrown for 29 TDs and nearly 3,000 yards. RB Caleb Hawkins has rushed for 1,081 yards and has added 424 yards receiving. Both WR Wyatt Young and WR Justin Bowick have over 750 receiving yards.

Since scoring just 10 points in Week 1 against Tulsa, Oklahoma State hasn't scored fewer than 32 over its last eight games. Texas Tech has given up at least 25 points in its last four games. The ingredients are very much there for a shootout.

No. 13 Wake Forest at SMU (-1.5) (Noon ET, ESPN): A win for Wake Forest puts the Demon Deacons in prime position for the ACC title game ahead of games vs. Georgia Tech and Duke. SMU isn't out of the ACC title picture either, and has No. 5 Notre Dame in Week 12. The Mustangs bounced back from a Halloween loss at Syracuse with a dominating Friday night win over Virginia Tech in Week 10.

Northwestern at No. 20 Ohio State (-12.5) (Noon ET, Fox): You have to go back to the 2011 season when Ohio State finished 6-7 to find the Buckeyes' last three-game losing streak. Northwestern's Aidan Chiles missed the Wildcats' loss to Iowa and his presence may be paramount to Northwestern's hopes of an upset. Northwestern had just 286 yards of offense on 69 plays against the Hawkeyes.

No. 8 Tennessee (-2.5) at Texas A&M (3 p.m. ET, ESPN): Yes, Texas A&M is just 1-5 in SEC play and still less than a field goal underdog to a top-10 opponent. That's how the SEC has gone this year. It wouldn't be surprising in the slightest to see the Aggies get the win as Tennessee is coming off a huge home win over Kentucky.

No. 22 Missouri at No. 1 Georgia (-15.5) (3:30 p.m. ET, ABC): The Tigers were still somehow ranked after losing at home to Texas and need wins over Georgia, Kentucky and Oklahoma to even have a hope of making the College Football Playoff. Florida at No. 11 Kentucky (-3.5) (6:15 p.m. ET, ESPN): The Wildcats are the last team provisionally in the playoff after their loss to the Volunteers. #2690. Cowboys have weapons to challenge the 49ers

The Cowboys moved to 4-5 with a dramatic 27-23 win over Indianapolis and now return home for one of their toughest tests of the season. San Francisco is 7-1, but Dallas enters Sunday having won two of its last three and is coming off a very productive offensive yardage performance.

Sure, the Dallas offense had issues scoring which was hampered by penalties and two critical turnovers, but they still produced 508 total yards.

Dallas outgained the Colts 508-271 yards on offense, producing 329 passing yards and another 179 on the ground. The Cowboys averaged 7.2 yards every time they snapped the football.

CeeDee Lamb was almost unstoppable in Indianapolis. He caught 10 passes for 195 yards and a touchdown, his second-highest receiving total in an NFL game. He now has 904 yards and seven touchdowns this season. San Francisco also left its latest game with cornerbacks Renardo Green and Deommodore Lenoir both day-to-day with injuries. If either is limited, Prescott should waste no time looking toward Lamb.

Javonte Williams also reached the century mark against Indianapolis, carrying 20 times for 101 yards and the game-winning touchdown. He now has 629 rushing yards and nine rushing touchdowns this season.

Keeping that balance is crucial against the 49ers. It slows down the pass rush and prevents San Francisco from simply attacking Prescott every down.

On the 49ers defense, Nick Bosa returned against Las Vegas, while DeForest Buckner made his return to San Francisco. Yet the 49ers finished the game with zero sacks. San Francisco have only 15 sacks entering that game, which is fourth-fewest in the NFL. The 49ers have dangerous names up front, but Dallas has reason to believe Prescott can be protected.

As for San Francisco's offense, it's dealing with a major injury problem. Christian Kirk has been placed on injured reserve. Mike Evans is not expected to be ready for this week, while Deebo Samuel is only expected to return to practice Wednesday after missing time with a hamstring injury.

That doesn't mean San Francisco lacks weapons. Christian McCaffrey and George Kittle remain major problems. But taking established receivers away from Brock Purdy makes the job easier for a Dallas secondary that has struggled this season.

If Dallas wants to beat San Francisco, slowing McCaffrey has to be near the top of the list. The encouraging part is what happened last Sunday. Jonathan Taylor entered the game as Indianapolis' biggest offensive weapon. Dallas held him to just 46 rushing yards. That was one of the Cowboys' best run-defense performances of the season.

McCaffrey presents a different challenge because of his receiving ability, but Dallas has at least shown it can stop a high-level running back from controlling a game.

So sticking with the Cowboys defense, Quinnen Williams forced a fumble last week, and rookie safety Caleb Downs grabbed his first NFL interception to seal the victory in the final minute. That comes after the defense produced five sacks and two takeaways against Arizona.

The 49ers are the heavy favorite, but the Cowboys have weapons that give the team at least a puncher's chance.

#2689. Sixers look to move past loss to Boston as they host Raptors

Despite sitting at a highly respectable 9-3 and featuring the star-studded starting five that had everyone doing backflips over the offseason, concerns are emanating around the Philadelphia 76ers. It's amazing what getting smacked around for the final quarter and a half against the Celtics will do to a team's vibes. Tuesday night also marked the Sixers' second 20-plus-point loss in their last three games, which doesn't overly inspire confidence.

I think it's important to remember for those suddenly down on the Sixers or ready to crown Boston that nothing is won in early November. Still, there are areas for improvement on both ends of the court for Philadelphia. The offense has struggled, sitting just 20th in the league in offensive rating as of this writing, taking on far too much of an iso-heavy look for my liking. It would also help for Joel Embiid to rediscover his shooting stroke, currently shooting just 37.0 percent from the field on the season. However, both Embiid (plantar fasciitis) and LeBron James (lower back) are listed as questionable on the injury report for tonight's contest against the Toronto Raptors. It's worrisome that those guys are listed as questionable when it's not even a back-to-back for the Sixers. Already without Adem Bona and Dominick Barlow (and Ariel Hukporti out for the season), the Sixers could be dangerously thin in the front court.

On the other side of the ball, the Sixers have been better than most expected on that side of the ball (8th in the league in defensive rating). The consistent failure to identify and close out on open shooters against Boston certainly raised some eyebrows, however. The rebounding has also been an issue when Embiid is on the bench, which could be a big problem if he's unable to go tonight.

By and large, though, they should have an easier time of things against Toronto, who have been around a league-average team thus far this season, but are at a schedule disadvantage after hosting Boston last night, a close 98-93 defeat in which the Raptors' offense went cold in the fourth quarter. While the Sixers' injury report could definitely be better, the Raptors are dealing with their own injury concerns. Kawhi Leonard is currently out while undergoing the reconditioning process for his knee. Scottie Barnes hasn't played since November 4 due to a groin injury. Reserve forward Trayce Jackson-Davis missed last night's game due to illness. In the absence of the two big stars, six Raptors scored between 11 and 17 points last night.

Tonight is unquestionably a good spot for the Sixers, facing a team traveling on the tail end of a back-to-back and missing their best two players. Still, if Philadelphia does end up missing two key starters of their own, victory will be far from assured. The remaining stars will need to pick up the scoring slack, most notably Tyrese Maxey and Jaylen Brown. Key reserves like Dean Wade and Jabari Walker will have to assume more of the burden on the boards in expanded roles. On the other hand, perhaps the starters are all able to suit up and the Sixers are able to earn that elusive comfortable win this season. Tune in tonight to find out.

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

This is an article version of the CBS Sports HQ AM Newsletter, the ultimate guide to every day in sports. You can sign up to get it in your inbox every weekday morning here.

One of the biggest benefits of the NIL era is that college basketball has more elite talent than ever, now that players are returning for bigger paychecks instead of bolting for NBA money at the first opportunity.

That made selecting our 2026-27 CBS Sports Preseason All-America teams especially difficult, but our experts nailed it. Each of the three teams features players who will be performing at the next level very soon, but the best of those might be Florida superstar Thomas Haugh.

As our own Isaac Trotter explains, if Haugh can improve his range shooting, he won't have to wait long to hear his name called in the 2027 NBA Draft.

When it comes to how the talent broke down by conference, it was a a pretty level playing field for the most part.

Not to spoil anyting, but Arizona freshman Caleb Holt did not make the cut. He did, however, turn some heads in the Wildcats' exhibition game.

Loyalty is an excellent quality to have in a friend or partner. It's also why we love dogs.

It should not be quite as prevalent among college football coaches, some of whom have been undone because they did what was comfortable, not what was necessarily best for the team.

Our own John Talty highlighted five high-profile coaches who have been loyal to a fault, making hires and personnel decisions that have come back to haunt them. One of those coaches is Mike Elko. After a shaky season from Marcel Reed in 2025, Texas A&M chose not to pursue an upgrade in the portal.

Instead, the Aggies gave Reed a major payday, and they'll miss the College Football Playoff because of it.

Look, it can happen to the best of us. Dan Lanning and Dabo Swinney wound up on the list, despite the success that those two have had throughout their careers.

Steve Sarkisian is another coach who has fallen into the trap of being too loyal, but he may have a huge decision on his hands in the offseason. Arch Manning has struggled enough that another year in college should be on the table. If that happens, would Sark welcome back Manning with open arms, despite his shortcomings?

Finally, one person for whom loyalty is no an issue is Missouri QB Austin Simmons. After Trinidad Chambliss won the starting job at Ole Miss last year, Simmons didn't feel the need to stick around, but there won't be bitterness when Simmons returns to Oxford this weekend.

#2685. Should the Phoenix Suns make a trade for Domantas Sabonis or Paolo Banchero?

Ten games into the 2026-27 NBA season, the trade rumors are already swirling around the Phoenix Suns.

While a vocal segment of the fanbase cries out for a point guard like the oft-injured Darius Garland, a new round of players have been linked to the Suns, amid questions of fit in their starting lineup.

After a couple of rounds of forced trades, from Deandre Ayton to Kevin Durant, and the financial strain of the Bradley Beal dead money, the Suns find themselves with a redundant starting lineup comprised of the best that their circumstance dictated they could get. This led to a lineup simultaneously redundant and lacking. Issues with size, consistency, and fit continue to hamper the Jordan Ott and the Suns as they struggle to allow their highest-dollar players to shine without drowning out the production of their teammates.

Last season ended with Brooks and Green eating up shots in the playoff series against the Thunder as Devin Booker was reduced to spraying the ball out of double teams and when Jalen Green or Dillon Brooks got hot it the ball got stuck leaving Book looking to box out instead of repositioning for a new angle of approach.

This season Booker is finding his shot. Against the Spurs, Book went on a vintage scoring heater, but down the vine the other grapes withered and dried like raisins in the sun, with only the Suns rookie Malauch notching over ten points for the night. Miles Bridges noted in the press conference that Booker got hot. A similar explanation Booker gave in the Thunder series after Jalen and Dillon put up big shot numbers in a loss. An alarming lack of synergy even early in the season.

The national media has picked up on the narrative and turned it into trade talk as Bleacher Report connected the Suns to four potential trade candidates: Darius Garland, Anthony Davis, Domantas Sabonis, and Paolo Banchero.

While none of these players are without their flaws, an argument could be made for each of them to be added to the Suns. But I urge fans to remember that the Suns are owned by Mat Ishbia, whose ownership style could be summed up in one word. Aggressive.

So while you may see a million Twitter posts arguing for which of the four would best improve the Suns' chances at winning a first-round playoff series, I say no. That's not enough, like Warren G's third album, I Want It All. Or at least half of it. Let me present my most recent fix for the Phoenix Suns roster woes.

Anthony Davis is a day away from street clothes every day. While the upside is clearest and highest on this list, I remind you that the most recent Suns' finals appearance was largely related to the availability of their key players. They rode that injury luck to a 2-0 lead in the NBA Finals before it finally caught up with them and Dario Saric went down, taking with him the Suns' best hope at closing out the Bucks. If there was one trade that had a chance to make the Suns a true title contender, it could be Anthony Davis, but history would suggest it's more likely he watches the Suns flounder from the bench.

Darius Garland trade rumors and mock trades have made their way around Suns Twitter since last season and continue to color me unimpressed by the proposition. The Suns have aligned themselves to be a defensive team. They traded away two of their best shooters in order to pursue a top-tier defense, and even if Garland was driving and kicking to open shooters, who would he be kicking it out to? It would be Book, Brooks, and Bridges instead of Grayson or Royce. There would be nights that will work, but plenty won't, and consistent three-point shooting won't be something the Suns can rely on to show up in four or five games of a seven-game series.

This leaves us with Sabonis and Banchero.

In the off-season, I explored the possibility of a Domantas Sabonis trade and was roundly derided as a lunatic by those who were curious enough to click the article. Now they all come crawling back as the Suns' rebounding woes, lack of size, and youth at the center position make a Sabonis trade far more palatable to the Suns masses.

I view Sabonis as a starting center-sized version of Oso Ighodaro. He sets great screens, facilitates like Oso, but brings more firepower scoring the ball and has long been one of the best rebounders in the game. Despite his individual defensive concerns, with the number of communication breakdowns leading to the Suns' defense giving up way too open shots, it could be argued that a veteran presence like Sabonis could initially improve the defense and the KhOso tandem gains experience.

While they may have to wait until the trade deadline, the trade I originally proposed of Jalen Green and Mark Williams still sounds like a winner in early November. While Sabonis would bring much-needed experience, size, and positional flexibility, allowing him to play next to the Suns' young centers, it wouldn't fix maybe the most glaring need of the Phoenix Suns alone. The need for a second star next to Booker.

Fall where you want on the PG debate, but I continue to side with the faction that believes the problem isn't necessarily the lack of a point guard but a second advantage creator next to Booker when teams try to take him off the board. Paolo, while once one of the bright young stars in the league, has fallen out of fashion in the NBA fan community. Yet, outside of Davis, he represents to me the most realistic chance of landing a bona fide All-Star next to Devin Booker.

Banchero's size, versatility as a ball handler, and ability to score inside the paint would flourish in the shadow of Book's gravity. Much like the Suns have struggled to assemble and retain the right mix of players around Devin Booker, the Magic couldn't add the shooting it needed to free up Paolo's downhill game. A fresh start and new roster could resurrect his once-rising star.

Adding both of them together could be the Suns' best option to meet Ishbia's lofty goal of a second-round playoff appearance in the once-again hotly contested Western Conference, so I hopped on the trade machine to cook up a new look for the Suns. One that plugs some holes in rebounding and facilitation and adds some much-needed upside to the Suns' playoff prospects in the 2026-27 season.

In order to complete the trade, the Suns must wait until some of their recently acquired players become eligible to move, but when February 11th hits, this is what I think the Suns should do.

#2684. For the third time, Camila Barros joins Brazil women's coaching staff

São Paulo will have another representative with the Brazilian Women's National Team for its final fixtures of 2026. Alongside defender Tayla, fitness coach Camila Barros will join Arthur Elias's coaching staff for the friendlies against Japan. The matches will take place on November 29 at Edion Peace Wing Stadium in Hiroshima and on December 5 at JFE Harenokuni Stadium in Okayama.

This is Camila's third call-up. Her first stint with the national team came in February 2025, during a training camp at Granja Comary in Rio de Janeiro state. She rejoined the staff in October 2026 and now has another opportunity to contribute to the national team.

"Working with the Brazilian National Team is a great learning opportunity, especially during this period of preparation for the World Cup. I see these stints as a chance to further develop my skills and bring that experience back to the club," she emphasized.

Camila's journey with the Tricolor began in 2017, when the club partnered with Centro Olímpico to compete in the São Paulo State Under-17 Championship. An Under-15 team was also formed at the time and won the state title. Following that work, the coaching staff and players were brought into São Paulo's youth setup on a permanent basis.

Camila started as a fitness coach in the club's youth ranks, working with the Under-16 and Under-17 teams from 2017 to 2021 and the Under-20 team in 2022. That same year, she joined São Paulo's senior women's team, where she has won major titles, including the 2025 Women's Super Cup and the 2026 Brazilian Women's Championship.

For her, those achievements helped open doors. "The work done by both the Health and Performance Department and the coaching staff was crucial to my call-ups. I believe the great work we have been building year after year, with important titles along the way, helped me earn these call-ups," she said.

Brazil will host the Women's World Cup for the first time, also marking the competition's debut in South America. The tournament will run from June 24 to July 25, 2027, featuring 32 national teams, 64 matches and eight host cities: Belo Horizonte, Brasília, Fortaleza, Porto Alegre, Recife, Rio de Janeiro, Salvador and São Paulo.

Camila also highlighted the excitement surrounding the country's hosting of the tournament.

"I believe everyone involved in women's football, especially in Brazil, is eager to see this major event take place in our country, with the chance to watch top national teams play up close. We know this is a great opportunity to take another step forward in developing and growing the women's game," she concluded.

#2682. Bears Question of the Day: What adjustment do you want to see after the Bye?

The Chicago Bears are 7-2 after Week 9 and sit atop the NFC North. With all context aside, you couldn't ask for a better position entering your bye week.

While the Bears do have some injuries that will hopefully heal up by Week 11 (namely Kyle Monangai and Luther Burden), the biggest thing the Bears can do is make necessary personnel adjustments to set themselves up for a deep playoff run.

For me, I think it's time to shuffle out Garrett Bradbury in favor of Logan Jones. While Bradbury has been mostly solid through the first 9 weeks, he's clearly the weak link on the OL and can lead to devastating results, as in the Bucs game. Pressure up the middle was constant during the Bears' nail-biting win, and the communication between Thuney, Jackson, and Bradbury is appearing as shaky as ever.

These types of plays require Bradbury to take authority as the Center and ensure the OL knows their assignments. Each and every week it is clearer that he isn't up to that task. Beyond the lack of communication, Bradbury seems to lack the lateral quickness and strength at the point of attack to win in run and pass reps.

This assembly of clips shows Bradbury frequently missing free rushers up the middle, getting beat at the point of attack, or lacking the athleticism to win downfield. It's consistently costing the Bears by forcing Caleb to get immediate pressure in his face, or limiting the effectiveness of the run game.

It hasn't been all bad for Bradbury, who has been a solid addition to a line that lost Drew Dalman to an early retirement. But it's time to bring in the rookie Logan Jones in relief.

Jones, who was selected in the 2nd round of the 2026 NFL draft, is the highest drafted OL for Ryan Poles since Darnell Wright. For a team looking to compete now, the expectation for a 2nd round pick should be for them to contribute sooner rather than later. Fortunately, Jones looked really good in his limited reps earlier this season against the Atlanta Falcons:

Seeing him seal off his man downfield and also win a few pass-blocking reps is highly encouraging. However, the rep at the 22 second mark of the link shows that he is still learning and is still prone to mistakes.

I am optimistic that if the Bears make this change after Week 11, and with their battering ram in Kyle Monangai returning, that the Bears can return to their elite rushing ways.

#2680. Neemias Queta is eager to give Celtics more without neglecting his core duties

Four games in six nights across four different cities, capped off by a back-to-back. For Celtics center Neemias Queta, that required 22.5 minutes per game, including a season-high 31 minutes in Wednesday night's road trip finale against the Raptors in Toronto.

Initially, Queta had no clue where to credit his critical source of energy.

"Not sure. I'm not sure," Queta told reporters after Boston's 98-93 win over Toronto, per CLNS Media.

But then, after shaking his head and cracking a smile as he thought about it, Queta credited those around him for their contagious approach.

"I think it's also energy plays from other teammates," Queta said.

Queta continued: "A lot of guys were making energy plays that galvanize your teammates, and we kind of fed from each other. And that's something we need to do more. It'll get us over the hump most nights."

The Celtics were without Paul George, their second-leading scorer, in Toronto as the 36-year-old sat out due to an illness less than 24 hours after dropping 36 points on the Sixers in Philadelphia. So that meant Boston had to pivot. Early on, however, it looked as though their first trip to The Six was shaping up to be a scheduled loss, despite the Raptors also being shorthanded without Kawhi Leonard and Scottie Barnes.

TORONTO, CANADA – NOVEMBER 11: Jakob Poeltl #19 of the Toronto Raptors take a tipoff against Neemias Queta #88 of the Boston Celtics in the first half of their NBA game at Scotiabank Arena on November 11, 2026 in Toronto, Ontario, Canada. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Cole Burston/Getty Images) | Getty Images

Boston's inability to contain Toronto's transition attack throughout the first half dug the Celtics into a hole, as they trailed by 22 points with 5:24 remaining until halftime. The Celtics responded with a 17-2 run of their own, cutting Toronto's lead down to 61-54 and giving the PG-13-less C's another chance to claw their way back with plenty of time to spare.

Still, there was plenty of more work to do.

Queta took only four shots throughout the night, including his third 3-point make of the season in the first quarter. He scored 11 points but recorded his first double-double of the campaign with 13 rebounds, which proved invaluable for the Celtics down the stretch.

He attempted four 3-pointers during the preseason, and has matched that total across the first 12 games of the regular season. It's something Queta truly believes he can work on, improve at, and add to his arsenal. But he's also aware that as a center, he still has fundamental responsibilities. So while pursuing that 3-point shot — among other strides — Queta understands he can't forsake his obligations to Boston's frontcourt.

"I think the game is so unpredictable nowadays that, like I've been saying over and over again, the more complete I can be, the more versatile I can be, the more I can play off others and they can be their best versions," he said. "I understand my teammates, and I can give them a relief in different aspects of the floor. Now it's just about me becoming more consistent in those things, whether it's shooting the ball, whether it's making reads with the ball in my hands, whether it's driving to the rim. I still need to be better."

In the final minute, Queta's commitment to those responsibilities became particularly valuable.

With less than 10 seconds on the shot clock, Jayson Tatum drove, drew two Raptors defenders and spotted Queta cutting to the basket for a wide-open dunk. That brought the Celtics within striking distance, trailing Toronto 93-92 with 54.1 seconds remaining.

TORONTO, CANADA – NOVEMBER 11: Jayson Tatum #0 of the Boston Celtics helps up Neemias Queta #88 in the second half of their NBA game at Scotiabank Arena on November 11, 2026 in Toronto, Ontario, Canada. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Cole Burston/Getty Images) | Getty Images

After Tatum knocked down back-to-back free throws on Boston's next possession, Queta's next — and biggest — heroic moment arrived, one that ultimately made all the difference for the Celtics.

He secured a crucial rebound after RJ Barrett missed his go-ahead layup attempt, preserving Boston's 94-93 lead. The Raptors immediately fouled Queta, sending him to the line, where he knocked down both free throws to extend the Celtics' lead to 96-93 with 15.1 seconds left.

That rebound wound up being a game-saver for Boston, helping the team extend its winning streak to five games and tie the Lakers for the NBA's best record at 10-2.

"He continues to get better and better as a player on both ends of the floor," Celtics head coach Joe Mazzulla told reporters. "Honestly, his offensive presence is just as impactful. Those two big free throws that he hit down the stretch, catching the ball in the seam, making plays. Defensively, he just lifts us to another level with the rim protection."

Teammates remain encouraged by Queta's continued improvements, following up his biggest breakthrough last season as a first-time starter.

"Neemi's been great for us," Derrick White told reporters. "He's grown so much these last few years, and he's a beast on both ends of the floor. Honestly, we ask a lot out of him offensively, and he just seems to always be in the right place, right time. Just expanding his game so much. We have so much trust in him."

Queta currently leads the Celtics in rebounds (6.2) and blocks (1.2) per game. He's also already surpassed his previous career highs in 3-pointers made and attempted in a single season, going 3-for-4 thus far, with plenty of basketball still ahead.

"We're gonna keep on getting better," Queta said, "and that's the mindset I have."

#2678. Aaron Rodgers grades Mike Tomlin's performance as analyst on NBC

Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers has made it explicitly clear that he wants nothing to do with the media or public life once he retires at the conclusion of this NFL season. But so long as microphones are still shoved in his face, Rodgers has no issue with expressing his opinions.

Rodgers and the Steelers are preparing to play the Cincinnati Bengals in a high-stakes AFC North battle on Sunday Night Football this week. Former Steelers head coach Mike Tomlin, who stepped down in January before joining NBC's Football Night In America this season, will be on site.

On Wednesday, ESPN's Brooke Pryor asked Rodgers about the Tomlin of it all.

"I still talk to him," Rodgers said. "I love Mike T, and I have so much appreciation for him bringing me here last year and the amount of fun that we had together. The closeness of the bond that we formed. So it'll be good to see him."

"I'm not surprised in the least," Rodgers said of Tomlin's post-NFL media stardom. "He is absolutely killing it on TV the few times I've seen him. Nobody can talk football better than Mike T, so it is an absolute match made in heaven. Him being on TV and doing what he does. And I don't know if he still wants to coach at some point, but he's doing a hell of a job."

Tomlin has been asked repeatedly about his desire to return to coaching in the NFL someday. On Wednesday, he was asked again during an NBC conference call.

"I'm having a lot of fun," Tomlin said, per Mark Maske of Front Office Sports. "Haven't given one iota of thought about coaching. I'm sure that some of that's going to come up in the not-too-distant future. But I'll cross that bridge when I come to it. Really haven't thought a lot about it. Really excited about my new role and working to get better each and every week."

Viewers overwhelmingly agree with Rodgers's review of Tomlin's broadcasting prowess. Tomlin's Steelers teams never finished with a losing record in his 19 years in Pittsburgh. Given the early returns on his first season on NBC, Tomlin is trending toward an indefinite winning streak as a media darling. My only complaint is having to wait indefinitely for Tomlin's next Minecraft City reveal video.

#2675. Alabama football Week 11 opponent preview: Vanderbilt Commodores

On Saturday afternoon, the Alabama Crimson Tide will play the final road game on their regular season schedule in Nashville against the Vanderbilt Commodores.

The Commodores are a team that has given Alabama problems the past two seasons, even upsetting the Tide back in 2024 in Nashville. Alabama avenged that loss a year ago in Tuscaloosa, and now enters this latest game between the two as a heavy favorite, even despite Vanderbilt having a number of players back from the two previous games.

Vanderbilt this season though has seen a number of struggles, and will come into this matchup owning a record that is under .500. A large number of those struggles have come in SEC action, though the Commodores are coming off a win in their most recent game, a result last week which snapped a previous five-game losing streak.

Here is everything you need to know about Vanderbilt ahead of Saturday's Week 11 showdown in Nashville.

Stadium: FirstBank Stadium, Nashville, Tennessee

Ranking: Unranked in CFP rankings, Unranked in US LBM Coaches Poll, Unranked in AP Poll

Vanderbilt currently sits at 4-5 overall (1-5 SEC) this season with wins against a trio of nonconference opponents in Austin Peay, Delaware, and NC State, as well as this past week on the road at Mississippi State. The Commodores at the moment are tied at the bottom of the SEC conference standings.

Clark Lea is currently in his sixth season as the head coach at Vanderbilt where he owns a combined 30-41 record dating back to 2021. The Commodores also have a pair of coordinators back this year from in Tim Beck and Steve Gregory on offense and defense, respectively.

Vanderbilt's offense is currently averaging only 23 points per game, a number which ranks third-fewest in the SEC. The Commodores also rank among the bottom half of the SEC in total, passing, and rushing yards per game.

The Commodores' defense is allowing an average of 29.4 points per game to their opponents, a number that ranks worst in the SEC. Vanderbilt also ranks among the bottom half of the SEC in total and rushing yards allowed a game to opponents, while the strength is their pass defense, which allows 221.3 yards per contest.

A large number of Vanderbilt's top offensive players to know return from last season such as Junior Sherrill, Sedrick Alexander, and Makhilyn Young, while kicker Brock Taylor is also back on special teams. Leading the Commodores' offense is true freshman quarterback Jared Curtis, a former top recruit last year's high school class.

#2673. Connor Hellebuyck trade: Jets send star goalie to the Devils in exchange for four players, two draft picks

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Connor Hellebuyck is a now a Devil. The star goalie for the Winnipeg Jets is on the move after being traded to New Jersey on Friday in exchange for four players and two future draft picks. the teams announced the move with the Jets receiving Dawson Mercer, Nick Bjugstad, Nico Daws and Alexander Command, plus a 2027 seventh-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick.

Hellebuyck expressed his desire to be traded in the offseason when he formally requested a move in August. He said at the time that he had made the request months earlier and tried to keep the situation private.

Hellebuyck has spent his entire career with Winnipeg after being drafted by the Jets in 2012 at No. 130 overall. He's recognized as one of the best goalies in the league as a three-time Vezina Trophy winner. He also helped carry the United States to its first gold medal since 1980 at the 2026 Olympics in February with some incredible saves against Canada in the final game.

After trading Jacob Markstom in the offseason, the Devils had a clear need in goal, and this splashy move certainly fills that need. With a talented young core already in place, New Jersey's Stanley Cup window is wide open.

RAISE HELLE!Connor Hellebuyck is a New Jersey Devil: https://t.co/HCehRGOQI5 pic.twitter.com/dZGNQR16m1

For the Jets, it must be a hard pill to swallow when a franchise icon decides to walk out they door, but this trade package should help them as the enter a new era and revamp the roster. Winnipeg got a former first-rounder in Mercer to try and add to a rebuild as well as a veteran presence in Bjugstad. They also acquired a younger goalie in Daws who could fill the role of Hellebuyck at just 25 years old.

Goaltending has been an issue in New Jersey for a while now -- even after the team acquired Markstrom from the Calgary Flames in 2024. Markstom never really panned out, and his 13.6 goals allowed above average, per Natural Stat Trick, were a big reason why the Devils missed the postseason last year.

In the early portion of this season, it was clear that New Jersey needed to make a move to upgrade in the crease. Daws and veteran Jake Allen simply aren't a tandem suitable for a Stanley Cup contender, and the numbers backed that up. New Jersey ranks 24th in team save percentage at .877, and the duo of Daws and Allen combined to surrender 2.99 goals above average.

Once Hellebuyck gets up to game speed, that shouldn't be a problem anymore.

In the three-season stretch from 2023-26, Hellebuyck led the NHL with 73.42 goals saved above average, which is 20 goals higher than the next closest netminder. Over that span, Hellebuyck also posted a standard save percentage of .914 and an astronomical high-danger save-percentage of .832.

Hellebuyck carried less talented teams to the playoffs multiple times in his career. Now on a team loaded with weaponry in their prime -- Jack Hughes, Jesper Bratt and Nico Hischier to name a few -- Hellebuyck could be the final piece to the championship puzzle.

In terms of the acquisition cost, it was probably an easy deal for Devils general manager Sunny Mehta to make. The 2029 second-round pick is useless for a team that should be all-in now, Bjugstad is simply a depth piece and Daws now has no path to a starting role with Hellebuyck in town.

The most interesting trade chips are Mercer and Command. Mercer flashed major upside with 56 points in his second NHL season, 2022-23, but he hasn't really come close to hitting those heights again. Still, even if he has plateaued, Mercer remains a strong middle-six forward rising into his prime.

Although Command had his detractors -- and may have been over-drafted at No. 12 overall -- he was a consensus first-round pick last summer. That gives Winnipeg a potential franchise forward it can build around long-term, but New Jersey already has one of the deepest forward groups in the league, especially with the emergence of Arseny Gritsyuk and the acquisition of Luke Evangelista.

If we're looking for a 3-D chess angle of this deal, it only makes the Devils more appealing for a certain Minnesota Wild defenseman whose brothers just happen to play in New Jersey already. Grade -- A+

Let's get the obvious out of the way first: The Jets were never going to get fair value for Hellebuyck because, at his best, he's the No. 1 goaltender in the world with no equal. That type of excellence can't be replaced.

That said, Winnipeg did fairly well given the circumstances. Hellebuyck made a public trade request, and he wasn't even with the team after sitting out for the entirety of training camp. The entire league knew the Jets had to trade him.

Hellebuyck's talent created a decent market anyway, but most of the suitors were bona fide Stanley Cup contenders with little in the way of valuable draft capital, and they weren't going to knee cap the roster by sending a key player back in return.

With all that taken into consideration, Kevin Cheveldayoff got a solid return. Although Mercer's ceiling may be lower than initially thought, he's a 24-year-old forward who banks roughly 20 goals and 20 assists every season. The kicker with Mercer will be Winnipeg's ability to re-sign him before he hits restricted free agency next summer.

The addition of Command means Winnipeg now has two forwards selected in the top 12 of the 2026 NHL Draft after taking center Viggo Bjorck themselves. If both of those players deliver on their first-round pedigrees, they could be a terrific one-two punch for the team long-term.

Daws was a third-round pick in 2020, and despite playing just 13 NHL games since the start of the 2024-25 season, he should give Winnipeg a solid back up option behind Stuart Skinner. It certainly helps that Skinner is off to a great start with his new team -- and if Daws develops into a true No. 1 -- it'll be gravy.

If there's any reason to critique this deal from the Jets' side of things, it's that they didn't get premium draft capital or a surefire up-and-coming prospect. Maybe Command develops into a star, but there's no guarantee he becomes a top-six stud in the NHL.

The Jets got a lot of good stuff, but they didn't really get anything great, at least not based on what we know in the moment. Because of that, I have to ding Winnipeg a little bit. Grade: B

#2672. Jaguars vs. Titans: Matchup History Through the Decades

Following their win last week during Thursday Night Football, the Jags will be on the road this Sunday in Nashville. Football has been fun lately, so it pains me to talk about the Tennessee Titans (fuck 'em). They're like taxes: you know it's happening every year and dread it, but persevere. The two teams have crossed paths 63 times, and the bad guys currently lead the series 35-28. While we hope we get another iconic Trevor stiff-arm moment, let's revisit the Titans losing at home against the Jaguars throughout the decades.

Week 10 on November 2, 1997Final score: Jaguars 30 – Oilers 24Attendance: 27, 208

The Titans were the Tennessee Oilers at this point in time, and this was their first loss to the Jags after leaving Texas. Chris Hudson, Pete Mitchell, and Mark Brunell scored touchdowns. Brunell completed 17 out of 31 attempted passes for 169 yards and was sacked three times for a loss of 14 yards. James Stewart led the team with 99 rushing yards, and Jimmy Smith led with 50 receiving yards. Mike Hollis made the three attempted field goals. Chris Hudson had a six-yard interception, and Steve McNair was sacked twice for a loss of 16 yards.

Week 10 on November 11, 2007Final score: Jaguars 28 – Titans 13Attendance: 69,143

I'm attempting to manifest another Week 10 win in Tennessee. Greg Jones, Maurice Jones-Drew, and Fred Taylor scored touchdowns. Quinn Gray completed 13 out of 23 attempted passes for 101 yards and was sacked once for a loss of five yards. Maurice Jones-Drew led the team with 101 rushing yards and 28 receiving yards, averaged 14.50 yards in kickoff returns, and averaged 14.00 yards in punt returns. Mike Peterson and Brian Williams intercepted two of Vince Young's passes. Reggie Hayward, Clint Ingram, and Jeremy Mincey sacked Young four times for a loss of 27 yards.

Week 13 on December 5, 2010Final score: Jaguars 17 – Titans 6Attendance: 69,143

Rashad Jennings and David Garrard scored touchdowns. Garrard completed 14 out of 19 attempted passes for 126 yards and was sacked once for a seven-yard loss. Maurice Jones-Drew led the team with 186 rushing yards, and Marcedes Lewis led with 36 receiving yards. Josh Scobee made one of the three attempted field goals. Derek Cox and William Middleton recorded interceptions. Jeremy Mincey recorded a sack on Kerry Collins for a loss of six yards. Rashean Mathis and Daryl Smith led the team with five combined tackles each.

Week 13 on November 30, 2025Final Score: Jaguars 25 – Titans 3Attendance: 54,098

The Titans scored their only points during the first quarter, and it was all Jacksonville football afterwards. Jakobi Meyers answered with a touchdown after a 50-yard catch-and-run brought the Jags to the five-yard line. Special teams forced a fumble and recovered the ball. Lawrence found Brenton Strange for another touchdown, then Trevor ran the two-point conversion in himself. In the second half, we saw a Tuten touchdown and a loose ball recovered by the Jags. Another game with Big Ham filling in at long snapper.

I promise to find something else to write about in two weeks. Please share what you dislike the most about the Titans with us in the comments or on social media.
